question.text: If the value of the integral <math><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo stretchy="false">∫</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>n</mi><mi></mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></math> is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the smallest prime number greater than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></math> is (where, <math><mi>s</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>n</mi><mi></mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> represents the signum function of <math><mi>x</mi></math>)
